source.text: דְּבַר־יְהוָ֣ה׀אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֗ה אֶל־מִיכָה֙ הַמֹּ֣רַשְׁתִּ֔י בִּימֵ֥י יוֹתָ֛ם אָחָ֥ז יְחִזְקִיָּ֖ה מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר־חָזָ֥ה עַל־שֹׁמְר֖וֹן וִירֽוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] word of Yahweh which came to Micah the Morashtite in [the] days of Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.

en.L: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} which came to Micah the Morashtite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s word came to Micah of Moresheth during the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah over Judah. It is what he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
en.R: This is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave to Micah from the town of Moresheth. It came while Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah. Micah saw these things about Samaria and Jerusalem.

es.L: Palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que vino a Miqueas el morastita en los días de Jotam, Acaz [y] Ezequías, reyes de Judá, la cual vio acerca de Samaria y de Jerusalén.
es.B: Este mensaje {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino a Miqueas de Moréset durante el reinado de Jotam, Acaz y Ezequías en Judá. Es lo que él vio acerca de Samaria y de Jerusalén.
es.R: Este es el mensaje que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio a Miqueas, del pueblo de Moréset. Le llegó cuando Jotam, Acaz y Ezequías eran reyes de Judá. Miqueas vio estas cosas acerca de Samaria y de Jerusalén.

fr.L: La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} qui fut adressée à Michée le Morashtite, aux jours de Jotham, d’Achaz, d’Ézéchias, rois de Juda, [parole] qu’il vit au sujet de Samarie et de Jérusalem.
fr.B: La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée à Michée de Morèsheth sous le règne de Jotham, d’Achaz et d’Ézéchias, rois de Juda. C’est ce qu’il vit au sujet de Samarie et de Jérusalem.
fr.R: Voici le message que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné à Michée, de la ville de Morèsheth. Ce message est venu quand Jotham, Achaz et Ézéchias étaient rois de Juda. Michée a vu ces choses au sujet de Samarie et de Jérusalem.

sw.L: Neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lililomjia Mika Mmoreshethi katika siku za Yothamu, Ahazi [na] Hezekia, wafalme wa Yuda, aliloliona kuhusu Samaria na Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilimjia Mika wa Moreshethi wakati wa utawala wa Yothamu, Ahazi na Hezekia, wafalme wa Yuda. Ndilo aliloliona kuhusu Samaria na Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Huu ndio ujumbe ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimpa Mika wa mji wa Moreshethi. Ulimjia wakati Yothamu, Ahazi na Hezekia walipokuwa wafalme wa Yuda. Mika aliona mambo haya kuhusu Samaria na Yerusalemu.

vi.L: Lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đến với Mi-chê người Mô-rê-sết trong đời Giô-tham, A-cha, Ê-xê-chia, các vua Giu-đa, là lời ông đã thấy về Sa-ma-ri và Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: Lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với Mi-chê người Mô-rê-sết dưới triều Giô-tham, A-cha và Ê-xê-chia, các vua Giu-đa. Đó là điều ông đã thấy về Sa-ma-ri và Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Đây là sứ điệp {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho Mi-chê, người thành Mô-rê-sết. Sứ điệp ấy đến khi Giô-tham, A-cha và Ê-xê-chia làm vua Giu-đa. Mi-chê đã thấy những điều này về Sa-ma-ri và Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: 유다의 왕들인 요담과 아하스와 히스기야의 시대에 모레셋 사람 미가에게 임한 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀, 곧 그가 사마리아와 예루살렘에 관하여 본 것이다.
ko.B: 이것은 요담과 아하스와 히스기야가 유다를 다스리던 때에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모레셋 사람 미가에게 주신 말씀이다. 그가 사마리아와 예루살렘에 관하여 본 것이다.
ko.R: 이것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모레셋 마을 출신의 미가에게 주신 말씀이다. 요담과 아하스와 히스기야가 유다의 왕이었을 때에 이 말씀이 임했다. 미가는 사마리아와 예루살렘에 관한 이 일들을 보았다.

decisions.choice: Micah the Morashtite: Micah from Moresheth, a town in the low hills southwest of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Micah is named after his home town, Moresheth-gath (1:14), in the low hill country between Judah's mountains and the Philistine plain, near Gath. Jeremiah 26:18 calls him by the same title and quotes 3:12. His name means "Who is like the LORD?", and the book ends by asking "Who is a God like you?" (7:18).

decisions.choice: in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah: the second half of the eighth century BC
decisions.reason: These three kings of Judah reigned one after another from about 750 to 686 BC (2 Kings 15:32-20:21). Micah was a younger contemporary of Isaiah and Hosea (Isaiah 1:1; Hosea 1:1). Samaria, the capital of the northern kingdom, fell to Assyria in 722 BC, and Assyria invaded Judah in 701 BC, in Hezekiah's reign. Jeremiah 26:18-19 says that Micah spoke in Hezekiah's days and that Hezekiah heeded him.

decisions.choice: which he saw: the word given to the prophet as something seen
decisions.reason: The verb is used for a prophet's vision, and books of prophecy use it of the whole message, words included (Isaiah 1:1; Amos 1:1). Samaria and Jerusalem were the capitals of the two kingdoms, Israel in the north and Judah in the south, and they stand for the two peoples. The book speaks to both.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD that came to (L); the LORD's word came to (B); This is the message the LORD gave to (R); during the reigns of (B); while ... were kings (R); of Moresheth (B); from the town of Moresheth (R)
decisions.reason: The heading follows the formula set for the first verse of each of the Twelve, as in Hosea 1:1 and Joel 1:1. Balanced and Readable name Micah's home town as Jeremiah 26:18 does at those levels, rather than use the word formed from it.

decisions.choice: "Palabra del SEÑOR que vino a" (L); "Este mensaje del SEÑOR vino a" (B); "Este es el mensaje que el SEÑOR le dio a" (R); "en los días de" (L); "durante el reinado de" (B); "cuando ... eran reyes" (R)
decisions.reason: The heading formula of the Twelve in Spanish, as in Hosea 1:1 and Jeremiah 1:1-2.

decisions.choice: "Miqueas el morastita" (L); "Miqueas de Moréset" (B); "del pueblo de Moréset" (R)
decisions.reason: The forms published in Spanish Jeremiah 26:18, where Micah is quoted.

decisions.choice: "La parole du SEIGNEUR qui fut adressée à Michée le Morashtite" (L); "La parole du SEIGNEUR fut adressée à Michée de Morèsheth" (B); "Voici le message que le SEIGNEUR a donné à Michée, de la ville de Morèsheth" (R), as the published Jeremiah 26:18 names him
decisions.reason: The heading formula the term sheet sets for the Twelve, and the name as the published Jeremiah 26:18 gives it at each level.

decisions.choice: Micah's and Nahum's oracles are speech at every level: present, future, and passé composé for the past, never passé simple; God's speech and the prophet's poetry take no quotation marks, words quoted inside them take « »; one city or people addressed as one person is "tu", a group "vous", switching where the Hebrew switches
alternatives: passé simple for past events in the oracles
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets for the prophets; the heading itself is narrative and keeps the passé simple at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: "Neno la BWANA lililomjia Mika Mmoreshethi katika siku za" (L); "Neno la BWANA lilimjia Mika wa Moreshethi wakati wa utawala wa" (B); "Huu ndio ujumbe ambao BWANA alimpa Mika wa mji wa Moreshethi" (R)
decisions.reason: The heading follows the form set for the books of the Twelve, as Jeremiah 1:1-2, and Micah is named as the published Swahili Jeremiah 26:18 names him at each level.

decisions.choice: Throughout Micah: "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}" for the divine name and "Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}" for the Lord GOD; God's oracles and the prophet's poetry take no quotation marks; deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives ("yake", "nami"), never on verb prefixes; "wewe" or "ninyi" as the Hebrew has one or many
decisions.reason: These are the settled Swahili choices for the prophets. Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb, where no capital is possible, so it has fewer deity_pronoun spans than the English.

decisions.choice: the book heading follows the terms note's form for Hosea, Joel, Micah and Zephaniah ("Lời của CHÚA đã đến với ... trong đời ..." L; "... dưới triều ..." B; "Đây là sứ điệp CHÚA ban cho ..." R), with "Mi-chê người Mô-rê-sết" as the published Jeremiah 26:18
decisions.reason: Book-wide choices for this job (Micah and Nahum), recorded once here: CHÚA is the divine-name span at every level; "the Lord GOD" is "Chúa là CHÚA"; God's oracles take no quotation marks; God says "các ngươi" to the people in rebuke; the prophet speaks as "tôi"; "nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên" (L, B) / "dân Y-sơ-ra-ên" (R); "con gái Si-ôn" (L, B) / "dân Si-ôn" (R); "những người sót lại" (L, B) / "những người còn sống sót" (R).

decisions.choice: "모레셋 사람 미가에게 임한 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀" (L); "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모레셋 사람 미가에게 주신 말씀" (B); "모레셋 마을 출신의 미가" (R)
decisions.reason: The heading follows the settled form for the Twelve, as Jeremiah 1:2, and names Micah as the published Korean Jeremiah 26:18 does. Korean puts the relative clauses before the noun, so Literal keeps the Hebrew's units rather than its order.

decisions.choice: Throughout Micah: every YHWH is "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}" and the Lord GOD "주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}"; God speaks in 해라체 with 나 and never gives himself -시-; the prophet speaks about God in the plain written style with -시- and 께서; oracles take no quotation marks; Korean has no deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: These are the settled Korean speech levels for the prophets. Korean has no capital letters, so respect for God is carried by the honorific -시-, 께서 and 그분 instead of deity_pronoun spans.

source.text: שִׁמְעוּ֙ עַמִּ֣ים כֻּלָּ֔ם הַקְשִׁ֖יבִי אֶ֣רֶץ וּמְלֹאָ֑הּ וִיהִי֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֤ה בָּכֶם֙ לְעֵ֔ד אֲדֹנָ֖י מֵהֵיכַ֥ל קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Hear, peoples, all of them; pay attention, earth and what fills it, and let be [the] Lord Yahweh against you for a witness, [the] Lord from [the] temple of his holiness.

en.L: Hear, peoples, all of them; \q pay attention, earth and all that fills it, \q and let the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} be a witness against you, \q the Lord from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy temple.
en.B: Listen, all you peoples; \q pay attention, earth and everything in it! \q Let the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} be a witness against you, \q the Lord from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy temple.
en.R: Listen, all you nations! \q Pay attention, earth and everyone on it! \q The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} will speak as a witness against you. \q The Lord speaks from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy temple.

es.L: {{plural_you:Oigan|Oíd}}, pueblos todos; \q presta atención, tierra, y todo lo que la llena, \q y que el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} sea testigo contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, \q el Señor desde {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santo templo.
es.B: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, pueblos todos; \q ¡presta atención, tierra, y todo lo que hay en ella! \q Que el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} sea testigo contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, \q el Señor desde {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santo templo.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, naciones todas! \q ¡Que preste atención la tierra y todos los que viven en ella! \q El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} hablará como testigo contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. \q El Señor habla desde {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santo templo.

fr.L: Écoutez, peuples, vous tous ; \q sois attentive, terre, et tout ce qui la remplit, \q et que le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} soit témoin contre vous, \q le Seigneur, depuis le temple de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} sainteté.
fr.B: Écoutez, vous tous, les peuples ; \q sois attentive, ô terre, avec tout ce qui s’y trouve ! \q Que le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} soit témoin contre vous, \q le Seigneur, depuis {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} saint temple.
fr.R: Écoutez, toutes les nations ! \q Fais attention, terre, avec tous ceux qui t’habitent ! \q Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} va témoigner contre vous. \q Le Seigneur parle depuis {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} saint temple.

sw.L: Sikieni, enyi watu, nyote; \q sikiliza, ee nchi, na vyote vilivyomo ndani yake, \q na Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} awe shahidi dhidi yenu, \q Bwana kutoka hekalu {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} takatifu.
sw.B: Sikilizeni, enyi mataifa yote; \q tega sikio, ee dunia, na kila kilichomo ndani yake! \q Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} na awe shahidi dhidi yenu, \q Bwana kutoka hekalu {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} takatifu.
sw.R: Sikilizeni, enyi mataifa yote! \q Sikiliza, ee dunia, pamoja na wote wanaoishi ndani yako! \q Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} atasema kama shahidi dhidi yenu. \q Bwana anasema kutoka hekalu {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} takatifu.

vi.L: Hỡi các dân, hết thảy hãy nghe; \q hỡi đất và mọi vật đầy dẫy trên đất, hãy lắng tai, \q và nguyện Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} làm chứng nghịch cùng các ngươi, \q là Chúa từ đền thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Hỡi muôn dân, hãy lắng nghe; \q hỡi đất và mọi loài trên đất, hãy chú tâm! \q Nguyện Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} làm chứng nghịch lại các ngươi, \q là Chúa ngự trong đền thánh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Hỡi các dân tộc, hãy lắng nghe! \q Hỡi đất và mọi người trên đất, hãy chú ý! \q Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ lên tiếng làm chứng nghịch lại các ngươi. \q Chúa phán từ đền thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 백성들아, 너희는 모두 들어라. \q 땅아, 그리고 그 안에 가득한 것들아, 귀를 기울여라. \q 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 너희에게 맞서는 증인이 되시기를, \q 그분의 거룩한 성전에서 주님께서 [증인이 되시기를].
ko.B: 모든 백성들아, 들어라. \q 땅과 그 안에 있는 모든 것아, 귀를 기울여라! \q 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 너희에게 맞서는 증인이 되시기를 바란다. \q 주님께서 그분의 거룩한 성전에서 증언하실 것이다.
ko.R: 모든 나라들아, 들어라! \q 땅과 그 위에 사는 모든 사람아, 귀를 기울여라! \q 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 너희를 고발하는 증인으로 말씀하실 것이다. \q 주님께서 그분의 거룩한 성전에서 말씀하신다.

decisions.choice: Hear, peoples, all of them: the same words as 1 Kings 22:28
decisions.reason: The prophet Micaiah son of Imlah ends his warning to King Ahab with these words (1 Kings 22:28; 2 Chronicles 18:27). Micah, whose name is a short form of Micaiah, opens his book with them. The call goes out to all the peoples and to the whole earth, as Isaiah 1:2 calls heaven and earth to listen.

decisions.choice: a witness against you: the Lord testifies against those he summons
decisions.reason: The words picture a court. The nations and the earth are called to hear, and the Lord himself takes the stand as witness. The preposition may mean "against you" or "among you". "Against" fits the court and the judgment that follows; the case the LORD brings is against Samaria and Jerusalem (verse 5), and the nations hear it as a warning that he judges the whole earth. The text does not say whether "you" means the peoples or Israel.

decisions.choice: his holy temple: the LORD's dwelling in heaven
decisions.reason: In the next verse the LORD comes out from "his place" and comes down to the earth, so the temple here is his dwelling above, as in Psalm 11:4 ("The LORD is in his holy temple; the LORD's throne is in heaven") and Habakkuk 2:20. The earthly temple in Jerusalem was its copy, and later in the book it too is judged (3:12).

decisions.choice: Hear, peoples, all of them (L); Listen, all you peoples (B); all you nations (R); all that fills it (L); everything in it (B); everyone on it (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the wording of 1 Kings 22:28 at those levels. Readable says "nations", the plain word for peoples, and turns the wish "let the Lord be a witness" into a statement of what he is about to do.

decisions.choice: "Oigan, pueblos todos" (L); "Escuchen, pueblos todos" (B), with plural_you
decisions.reason: The words are those of 1 Kings 22:28, so they reuse its published Spanish; the peoples are addressed as a group, the earth as one.

decisions.choice: "el Señor DIOS" for Adonai YHWH, the article outside the span
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets for "the Lord GOD" throughout the prophets.

decisions.choice: "Écoutez, peuples, vous tous", the published 1 Kings 22:28
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew words as the other Micaiah's cry in 1 Kings 22:28, as the English meaning decision notes; Literal reuses the published wording.

decisions.choice: "le Seigneur DIEU", with only DIEU under the divine_name setting, for Adonai YHWH throughout Micah
decisions.reason: As published Isaiah and Jeremiah and the term sheet.

decisions.choice: "Sikieni, enyi watu, nyote" (L); "Sikilizeni, enyi mataifa yote" (B)
decisions.reason: Each level reuses the published Swahili 1 Kings 22:28 at that level, the words Micaiah spoke (m1).

decisions.choice: "Chúa là CHÚA" for "the Lord GOD" (Adonai YHWH), at every level
decisions.reason: The terms note: "Chúa" is plain text outside the span and never in capitals; the span is on CHÚA alone, as in Isaiah 28:16.

decisions.choice: "đền thánh" for "his holy temple"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: the LORD's dwelling in heaven; "đền thánh" is the published Psalms wording and does not point to the Jerusalem building only.

decisions.choice: "주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서" with 께서 after the span
decisions.reason: 하나님 ends in a consonant and 야훼 in a vowel, so only particles that read right after both (께서, 께, 의, 도, 에게) follow the span; this holds through Micah. "Adonai" alone is "주님".

source.text: כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה יֹצֵ֣א מִמְּקוֹמ֑וֹ וְיָרַ֥ד וְדָרַ֖ךְ עַל־בָּ֥מֳתֵי אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: For look, Yahweh [is] going out from his place, and he will come down and tread on [the] high places of [the] earth.

en.L: For look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is coming out from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come down and tread on the earth's heights.
en.B: See, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is coming out from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dwelling; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come down and tread on the heights of the earth.
en.R: Look! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is leaving {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home in heaven. \q He will come down and walk on the high places of the earth.

es.L: Porque he aquí, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} sale de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} lugar, \q y descenderá y pisará las alturas de la tierra.
es.B: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} sale de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} morada; \q descenderá y pisará las alturas de la tierra.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}! {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} deja {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} hogar en el cielo. \q Descenderá y caminará sobre los lugares altos de la tierra.

fr.L: Car voici, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} sort de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} lieu, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} descendra et marchera sur les hauteurs de la terre.
fr.B: Voici, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} sort de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} demeure ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} va descendre et marcher sur les hauteurs de la terre.
fr.R: Regardez ! {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} quitte {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} demeure dans le ciel. \q Il va descendre et marcher sur les sommets de la terre.

sw.L: Kwa maana tazama, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anatoka mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}}, \q {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atashuka na kukanyaga mahali palipoinuka pa dunia.
sw.B: Tazama, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anatoka katika makao {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}; \q atashuka na kukanyaga vilele vya dunia.
sw.R: Tazama! {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anaondoka nyumbani {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} mbinguni. \q Atashuka na kutembea juu ya mahali pa juu pa dunia.

vi.L: Vì kìa, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang ra khỏi chỗ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ ngự xuống và giẫm trên các nơi cao của đất.
vi.B: Kìa, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang ra khỏi nơi ngự của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ ngự xuống và bước đi trên các đỉnh cao của đất.
vi.R: Hãy xem! {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang rời nơi ngự của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên trời. \q Ngài sẽ ngự xuống và bước đi trên các nơi cao của đất.

ko.L: 보라, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분의 처소에서 나오신다. \q 그분께서 내려오셔서 땅의 높은 곳들을 밟으실 것이다.
ko.B: 보아라, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분의 거처에서 나오신다. \q 그분께서 내려오셔서 땅의 높은 곳들을 밟으실 것이다.
ko.R: 보아라! {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하늘에 있는 그분의 집을 떠나신다. \q 그분께서 내려오셔서 땅의 높은 곳 위를 걸으실 것이다.

decisions.choice: tread on the heights of the earth: the words of Amos 4:13, where the LORD is the Creator who walks over the mountains
decisions.reason: Amos uses the same phrase in a hymn to the LORD as Creator (Amos 4:13), and Deuteronomy 32:13 and 33:29 speak of riding or treading on the heights as a mark of mastery. To tread on the heights is to rule over the whole earth. When the LORD comes down, the earth cannot bear his coming (verse 4).

decisions.choice: high places: the heights of the land, with a hint of the hilltop shrines
decisions.reason: The word means heights or ridges. It is also the usual word for the hilltop shrines where Israel and Judah worshiped, often with idols, and verse 5 uses it in that sense: "the high places of Judah". The LORD comes down onto the very heights where he is falsely worshiped.

decisions.choice: coming out from his place: the LORD comes to judge
decisions.reason: "His place" is his dwelling in heaven (verse 2). Scripture often pictures God coming down to see and to act (Genesis 11:5; Exodus 19:18-20; Isaiah 26:21, where he comes "out of his place" to punish the earth). Here his coming is a judgment: the mountains melt under him.

decisions.choice: the earth's heights (L), the heights of the earth (B), walk on the high places of the earth (R), as Amos 4:13; his home in heaven (R)
decisions.reason: Each level reuses its wording of Amos 4:13. Readable says where "his place" is (m3).

decisions.choice: "{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}" (B, R); "he aquí" (L)
decisions.reason: The call to look is made to the peoples of verse 2, so Balanced and Readable use the plural form with the plural_you setting.

source.text: וְנָמַ֤סּוּ הֶֽהָרִים֙ תַּחְתָּ֔יו וְהָעֲמָקִ֖ים יִתְבַּקָּ֑עוּ כַּדּוֹנַג֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הָאֵ֔שׁ כְּמַ֖יִם מֻגָּרִ֥ים בְּמוֹרָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And will melt the mountains under him, and the valleys will split open, like wax before the fire, like water poured down on a slope.

en.L: And the mountains will melt under {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and the valleys will split open, \q like wax before the fire, \q like water poured down a slope.
en.B: The mountains will melt beneath {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and the valleys will burst apart, \q like wax before the fire, \q like water rushing down a steep slope.
en.R: The mountains will melt under {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet. \q The valleys will split open. \q The mountains will melt like wax near a fire. \q The valleys will pour away like water rushing down a hill.

es.L: Y se derretirán los montes debajo de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, \q y los valles se hendirán, \q como la cera delante del fuego, \q como las aguas derramadas por una pendiente.
es.B: Los montes se derretirán bajo {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, \q y los valles se partirán, \q como la cera ante el fuego, \q como el agua que se precipita por una cuesta empinada.
es.R: Los montes se derretirán bajo {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies. \q Los valles se abrirán. \q Los montes se derretirán como la cera cerca del fuego. \q Los valles se escurrirán como el agua que baja corriendo por una colina.

fr.L: Et les montagnes fondront sous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, \q et les vallées se fendront, \q comme la cire devant le feu, \q comme des eaux versées sur une pente.
fr.B: Les montagnes fondront sous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, \q et les vallées éclateront, \q comme la cire devant le feu, \q comme l’eau qui dévale une pente raide.
fr.R: Les montagnes fondront sous {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds. \q Les vallées s’ouvriront. \q Les montagnes fondront comme de la cire près du feu. \q Les vallées s’écouleront comme de l’eau qui dévale une colline.

sw.L: Na milima itayeyuka chini {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \q na mabonde yatapasuka, \q kama nta mbele ya moto, \q kama maji yaliyomwagwa kwenye mteremko.
sw.B: Milima itayeyuka chini {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \q na mabonde yatapasuka, \q kama nta mbele ya moto, \q kama maji yanayoporomoka kwenye mteremko mkali.
sw.R: Milima itayeyuka chini ya miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \q Mabonde yatapasuka. \q Milima itayeyuka kama nta karibu na moto. \q Mabonde yatatiririka kama maji yanayoshuka kwa kasi kutoka kilimani.

vi.L: Các núi sẽ tan chảy dưới {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q và các thung lũng sẽ nứt ra, \q như sáp trước lửa, \q như nước đổ xuống dốc.
vi.B: Núi non sẽ tan chảy dưới chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q và thung lũng sẽ nứt toác, \q như sáp chảy trước lửa, \q như nước đổ ào xuống sườn dốc.
vi.R: Núi non sẽ tan chảy dưới chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Thung lũng sẽ nứt ra. \q Núi tan chảy như sáp gần lửa. \q Thung lũng trôi đi như nước chảy xiết xuống đồi.

ko.L: 그리고 산들이 그분 아래에서 녹고 \q 골짜기들이 갈라질 것이다. \q 불 앞의 밀랍 같고, \q 비탈로 쏟아지는 물 같을 것이다.
ko.B: 산들이 그분 아래에서 녹아내리고, \q 골짜기들이 터져 갈라질 것이다. \q 불 앞의 밀랍처럼, \q 가파른 비탈로 쏟아져 내리는 물처럼.
ko.R: 산들이 그분의 발아래에서 녹을 것이다. \q 골짜기들이 갈라질 것이다. \q 산들은 불 가까이에 놓인 밀랍처럼 녹을 것이다. \q 골짜기들은 언덕 아래로 쏟아져 내리는 물처럼 쓸려 갈 것이다.

decisions.choice: mountains melting like wax: a picture used when God comes
decisions.reason: Psalm 97:5 says that the mountains melt like wax before the LORD, and Judges 5:4-5 and Psalm 68:9 tell how the earth shook when God came out from Sinai. Nahum 1:5 uses the same picture. Nothing in creation stands firm when its maker comes to judge.

decisions.choice: like wax ... like water: the first likeness goes with the mountains, the second with the valleys
decisions.reason: Hebrew poetry often matches two pictures with two things in order. The mountains melt like wax in a fire, and the valleys split open as water cuts a channel when it pours down a slope.

decisions.choice: under his feet; The mountains will melt ... The valleys will pour away (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says which likeness goes with which part of the land (m2), so that the two pictures are not left floating. "Under his feet" says what "under him" means when he treads on the heights (verse 3).

source.text: בְּפֶ֤שַׁע יַֽעֲקֹב֙ כָּל־זֹ֔את וּבְחַטֹּ֖אות בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִֽי־פֶ֣שַׁע יַעֲקֹ֗ב הֲלוֹא֙ שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן וּמִי֙ בָּמ֣וֹת יְהוּדָ֔ה הֲל֖וֹא יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For [the] transgression of Jacob [is] all this, and for [the] sins of [the] house of Israel. Who [is the] transgression of Jacob? [Is it] not Samaria? And who [are the] high places of Judah? [Is it] not Jerusalem?

en.L: All this [is] for the transgression of Jacob \q and for the sins of the house of Israel. \q Who [is] the transgression of Jacob? [Is it] not Samaria? \q And who [are] the high places of Judah? \q [Are they] not Jerusalem?
en.B: All this is because of Jacob's rebellion \q and because of the sins of the house of Israel. \q What is Jacob's rebellion? Is it not Samaria? \q And what are Judah's high places? \q Are they not Jerusalem?
en.R: All this will happen because the people of Jacob have sinned, \q because the people of Israel have done wrong. \q Who is to blame for Jacob's sin? Is it not Samaria? \q Who is to blame for Judah's hilltop shrines? \q Is it not Jerusalem?

es.L: Por la transgresión de Jacob [es] todo esto, \q y por los pecados de la casa de Israel. \q ¿Quién [es] la transgresión de Jacob? ¿No [es] Samaria? \q ¿Y quiénes [son] los lugares altos de Judá? \q ¿No [es] Jerusalén?
es.B: Todo esto es por el delito de Jacob \q y por los pecados de la casa de Israel. \q ¿Cuál es el delito de Jacob? ¿No es Samaria? \q ¿Y cuáles son los lugares altos de Judá? \q ¿No es Jerusalén?
es.R: Todo esto sucederá porque el pueblo de Jacob ha pecado, \q porque el pueblo de Israel ha hecho lo malo. \q ¿Quién tiene la culpa del pecado de Jacob? ¿No es Samaria? \q ¿Quién tiene la culpa de los santuarios de las colinas de Judá? \q ¿No es Jerusalén?

fr.L: Pour la transgression de Jacob [est] tout cela, \q et pour les péchés de la maison d’Israël. \q Qui [est] la transgression de Jacob ? N’[est-ce] pas Samarie ? \q Et qui [sont] les hauts lieux de Juda ? \q N’[est-ce] pas Jérusalem ?
fr.B: Tout cela arrive à cause de la rébellion de Jacob \q et à cause des péchés de la maison d’Israël. \q Quelle est la rébellion de Jacob ? N’est-ce pas Samarie ? \q Et quels sont les hauts lieux de Juda ? \q N’est-ce pas Jérusalem ?
fr.R: Tout cela arrivera parce que le peuple de Jacob a péché, \q parce que le peuple d’Israël a fait le mal. \q Qui est responsable du péché de Jacob ? N’est-ce pas Samarie ? \q Qui est responsable des sanctuaires sur les collines de Juda ? \q N’est-ce pas Jérusalem ?

sw.L: Kwa ajili ya maasi ya Yakobo [ni] haya yote, \q na kwa ajili ya dhambi za nyumba ya Israeli. \q Maasi ya Yakobo ni nani? Je, si Samaria? \q Na mahali pa juu pa Yuda ni nani? \q Je, si Yerusalemu?
sw.B: Haya yote ni kwa sababu ya makosa ya Yakobo \q na kwa sababu ya dhambi za nyumba ya Israeli. \q Makosa ya Yakobo ni nini? Je, si Samaria? \q Na mahali pa juu pa Yuda ni nini? \q Je, si Yerusalemu?
sw.R: Haya yote yatatokea kwa sababu watu wa Yakobo wametenda dhambi, \q kwa sababu watu wa Israeli wamefanya maovu. \q Ni nani wa kulaumiwa kwa dhambi ya Yakobo? Je, si Samaria? \q Ni nani wa kulaumiwa kwa mahali pa ibada vilimani pa Yuda? \q Je, si Yerusalemu?

vi.L: Mọi điều này [là] vì tội vi phạm của Gia-cốp \q và vì tội lỗi của nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên. \q Ai [là] tội vi phạm của Gia-cốp? Chẳng phải Sa-ma-ri sao? \q Ai [là] những nơi cao của Giu-đa? \q Chẳng phải Giê-ru-sa-lem sao?
vi.B: Mọi điều ấy là vì tội ác của Gia-cốp \q và vì tội lỗi của nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên. \q Tội ác của Gia-cốp là gì? Chẳng phải là Sa-ma-ri sao? \q Những nơi cao của Giu-đa là gì? \q Chẳng phải là Giê-ru-sa-lem sao?
vi.R: Mọi điều này sẽ xảy ra vì dân Gia-cốp đã phạm tội, \q vì dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã làm điều sai trái. \q Ai phải chịu trách nhiệm về tội của Gia-cốp? Chẳng phải Sa-ma-ri sao? \q Ai phải chịu trách nhiệm về các miếu thờ trên đồi của Giu-đa? \q Chẳng phải Giê-ru-sa-lem sao?

ko.L: 이 모든 것은 야곱의 반역 때문이고, \q 이스라엘 집의 죄들 때문이다. \q 야곱의 반역이 누구냐? 사마리아가 아니냐? \q 유다의 산당들이 누구냐? \q 예루살렘이 아니냐?
ko.B: 이 모든 일은 야곱의 반역 때문이고, \q 이스라엘 집의 죄 때문이다. \q 야곱의 반역이 무엇이냐? 사마리아가 아니냐? \q 유다의 산당이 무엇이냐? \q 예루살렘이 아니냐?
ko.R: 이 모든 일이 일어나는 것은 야곱 백성이 죄를 지었기 때문이다. \q 이스라엘 백성이 악한 일을 했기 때문이다. \q 야곱의 죄는 누구 탓이냐? 사마리아가 아니냐? \q 유다의 산꼭대기 제단들은 누구 탓이냐? \q 예루살렘이 아니냐?

decisions.choice: Who is the transgression of Jacob? The capital cities are named as the source of the nation's sin
decisions.reason: The question asks "who", not "what": the sin is identified with a place and its people. Samaria and Jerusalem, the capitals where the kings, the officials and the chief shrines were, are where the wrong began and from where it spread. Here "Jacob" pairs with Samaria and means the northern kingdom, and Judah pairs with Jerusalem. In the first half of the verse "Jacob" and "the house of Israel" may mean the whole people.

decisions.choice: transgression: rebellion, a breaking of faith with God
decisions.reason: The word means a revolt, the act of a subject who breaks away from his overlord (2 Kings 8:20). Used of Israel, it is rebellion against the LORD, who made a covenant with them. Verse 13 and 3:8 use it again.

decisions.choice: the high places of Judah: as the Hebrew text has it
alternatives: the sin of the house of Judah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "the high places of Judah", the hilltop shrines (see verse 3). The ancient Greek translation and some other ancient versions read "the sin of the house of Judah", which matches the first half of the verse more closely. The Hebrew is the harder reading, and it fits the charge in verse 7 that the shrines were places of idolatry, so it is kept.

decisions.choice: transgression (L); rebellion (B); sin (R); high places (L, B); hilltop shrines (R); Who is to blame for (R)
decisions.reason: The word for transgression follows the wording set for the prophets. Readable says what the high places were and puts the question "who is ...?" as "who is to blame for ...?", which is its point (m1). Balanced asks "what", as English would, since a city is named in the answer.

decisions.choice: "transgresión" (L); "delito" (B); "pecado" (R), here and through Micah
decisions.reason: The settled Spanish for peshaʿ in the prophets (term sheet), where the English Balanced has "rebellion".

decisions.choice: "los lugares altos" (L, B); "los santuarios de las colinas" (R)
decisions.reason: As published Kings and Hosea 10:8.

decisions.choice: peshaʿ "transgression" (L), "rébellion" (B), "péché" (R); high places "hauts lieux" (L, B), "sanctuaires sur les collines" (R), for the whole of Micah
decisions.reason: As the term sheet; Balanced takes "rébellion" from its range because the English Balanced says "rebellion".

decisions.choice: "maasi" (L); "makosa" (B); "dhambi" (R) for pesha', here and through Micah; "mahali pa juu" (L, B), "mahali pa ibada vilimani" (R) for the high places
decisions.reason: The words for transgression are those settled for the prophets, as Psalm 51:3. Readable says what the high places were, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "tội vi phạm" (L); "tội ác" (B); "tội" (R) for "pesha'"
decisions.reason: The terms note's wording for "pesha'" in the Twelve, kept through Micah.

decisions.choice: "Ai [là] ...?" kept at Literal
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: the capital cities are named as the source of sin, so the Hebrew "who" points to the people of those cities; Literal keeps it, Balanced asks "là gì", Readable asks who is to blame.

decisions.choice: "반역" (L, B); "죄" (R) for pesha'; "산당" (L, B), "산꼭대기 제단" (R) for the high places, through Micah
decisions.reason: These are the settled Korean words for the prophets, as Kings has 산당. Literal keeps the question "누구냐" (who), as the Hebrew asks (m1).

source.text: וְשַׂמְתִּ֥י שֹׁמְר֛וֹן לְעִ֥י הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה לְמַטָּ֣עֵי כָ֑רֶם וְהִגַּרְתִּ֤י לַגַּי֙ אֲבָנֶ֔יהָ וִיסֹדֶ֖יהָ אֲגַלֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make Samaria into a heap of ruins of the field, into planting places of a vineyard; and I will pour down to the valley her stones, and her foundations I will uncover.

en.L: And I will make Samaria a heap of ruins in the field, a place for planting vineyards; \q and I will pour down her stones into the valley \q and uncover her foundations.
en.B: So I will make Samaria a heap of rubble in the open country, a place for planting vineyards. \q I will hurl her stones down into the valley \q and lay her foundations bare.
en.R: So I will turn Samaria into a pile of rubble in an open field, a place to plant grapevines. \q I will roll the stones of her buildings down into the valley \q and leave her foundations showing.

es.L: Y haré de Samaria un montón de ruinas del campo, un lugar para plantar viñas; \q y derramaré sus piedras en el valle \q y descubriré sus cimientos.
es.B: Por eso haré de Samaria un montón de escombros en campo abierto, un lugar para plantar viñas. \q Lanzaré sus piedras al valle \q y dejaré al descubierto sus cimientos.
es.R: Por eso convertiré a Samaria en un montón de escombros en medio del campo, un lugar para plantar viñas. \q Haré rodar las piedras de sus edificios hasta el valle \q y dejaré a la vista sus cimientos.

fr.L: Et je ferai de Samarie un monceau de ruines des champs, un lieu à planter de la vigne ; \q et je ferai dévaler ses pierres dans la vallée, \q et je mettrai à nu ses fondations.
fr.B: Je ferai donc de Samarie un tas de décombres en pleine campagne, un terrain pour planter des vignes. \q Je précipiterai ses pierres dans la vallée \q et je mettrai à nu ses fondations.
fr.R: Je vais faire de Samarie un tas de pierres au milieu d’un champ, un endroit où l’on plante des vignes. \q Je ferai rouler les pierres de ses maisons jusque dans la vallée, \q et on verra ses fondations.

sw.L: Na nitaifanya Samaria kuwa rundo la magofu ya shambani, mahali pa kupanda mizabibu; \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitayamwaga mawe yake bondeni, \q na kuifunua misingi yake.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo nitaifanya Samaria kuwa rundo la kifusi mashambani, mahali pa kupanda mizabibu. \q Nitayavurumisha mawe yake bondeni \q na kuiacha misingi yake wazi.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nitaigeuza Samaria kuwa rundo la kifusi katikati ya shamba, mahali pa kupanda mizabibu. \q Nitayaviringisha mawe ya majengo yake hadi bondeni, \q na misingi yake itaonekana.

vi.L: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho Sa-ma-ri thành một đống đổ nát ngoài đồng, một nơi để trồng vườn nho; \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đổ đá của nó xuống thung lũng \q và phơi trần nền móng của nó.
vi.B: Vì vậy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ biến Sa-ma-ri thành một đống gạch vụn giữa đồng trống, một chỗ để trồng nho. \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ném đá của nó xuống thung lũng \q và phơi trần nền móng nó ra.
vi.R: Vì vậy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ biến Sa-ma-ri thành một đống gạch đá vụn giữa cánh đồng, một chỗ để trồng nho. \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ lăn đá của các tòa nhà trong thành xuống thung lũng \q và để lộ nền móng của nó ra.

ko.L: 내가 사마리아를 들판의 폐허 더미로, 포도나무를 심는 곳으로 만들 것이다. \q 내가 그 돌들을 골짜기로 쏟아 내리고, \q 그 기초를 드러낼 것이다.
ko.B: 그러므로 내가 사마리아를 빈 들의 돌무더기로, 포도원을 일굴 땅으로 만들겠다. \q 그 돌들을 골짜기로 내던지고 \q 그 기초를 드러내겠다.
ko.R: 그래서 내가 사마리아를 들판 한가운데의 돌무더기로, 포도나무를 심는 곳으로 바꾸어 놓겠다. \q 그 성의 건물 돌들을 골짜기로 굴려 내리고, \q 그 기초가 드러나게 하겠다.

decisions.choice: I will make: the LORD now speaks
decisions.reason: Verses 2-5 speak about the LORD; here he speaks himself, as often in the prophets, without a formula to mark the change. The poem's "I" is the LORD until verse 8, where the prophet speaks of his own grief.

decisions.choice: Samaria will become a field for vineyards: the city on its hill will be leveled
decisions.reason: Samaria stood on a hill with steep sides (1 Kings 16:24). Its stones will be tumbled down the slopes into the valley below, and the hilltop will be fit only for planting vines, like any open field. Samaria fell to Assyria in 722 BC (2 Kings 17:5-6). "Her" is the city, which Hebrew speaks of as a woman.

decisions.choice: a heap of ruins (L); a heap of rubble (B); a pile of rubble (R); pour down (L); hurl (B); roll the stones of her buildings (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to pour out, here of stones tipped over the edge of the hill. Balanced says "hurl" and Readable "roll", and Readable says that the stones are the city's buildings.

decisions.choice: the LORD now speaks as "Ta" (spanned), and Samaria is "nó"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: God speaks from this verse. The terms note: a city is "nó" in the oracles; the feminine images of verse 7 do not make Samaria "nàng", which the note keeps for Zion.

decisions.choice: The LORD now speaks in 해라체 with "내가", without -시-
decisions.reason: The poem turns to God's own speech without a formula (m1), so the speech level changes with the speaker.

source.text: וְכָל־פְּסִילֶ֣יהָ יֻכַּ֗תּוּ וְכָל־אֶתְנַנֶּ֨יהָ֙ יִשָּׂרְפ֣וּ בָאֵ֔שׁ וְכָל־עֲצַבֶּ֖יהָ אָשִׂ֣ים שְׁמָמָ֑ה כִּ֠י מֵאֶתְנַ֤ן זוֹנָה֙ קִבָּ֔צָה וְעַד־אֶתְנַ֥ן זוֹנָ֖ה יָשֽׁוּבוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And all her carved images will be beaten to pieces, and all her hires will be burned with fire, and all her idols I will make a desolation; for from [the] hire of a prostitute she gathered [them], and to [the] hire of a prostitute they will return.

en.L: And all her carved images will be beaten to pieces, and all her wages will be burned with fire, \q and all her idols I will make a desolation; \q for from the wages of a prostitute she gathered [them], \q and to the wages of a prostitute they will return.
en.B: All her carved idols will be smashed to pieces, all her temple gifts burned in the fire, \q and I will lay waste all her images. \q For she collected them from a prostitute's pay, \q and they will go back to be a prostitute's pay.
en.R: All her idols will be smashed, and all the gifts given at her shrines will be burned. \q I will destroy all her false gods. \q She got them the way a prostitute gets her pay, \q and they will be used again to pay prostitutes.

es.L: Y todas sus imágenes talladas serán hechas pedazos, y todas sus ganancias serán quemadas en el fuego, \q y de todos sus ídolos haré una desolación; \q porque de la paga de prostituta [los] juntó, \q y a la paga de prostituta volverán.
es.B: Todos sus ídolos tallados serán hechos añicos, y todas las ofrendas de sus templos serán quemadas en el fuego, \q y arrasaré todas sus imágenes. \q Porque los reunió con la paga de una prostituta, \q y volverán a ser paga de prostituta.
es.R: Todos sus ídolos serán destrozados, y todos los regalos que se dieron en sus santuarios serán quemados. \q Destruiré todos sus dioses falsos. \q Los consiguió como una prostituta consigue su paga, \q y se usarán otra vez para pagar a prostitutas.

fr.L: Et toutes ses statues taillées seront mises en pièces, et tous ses salaires seront brûlés au feu, \q et de toutes ses idoles je ferai une désolation ; \q car c’est avec le salaire d’une prostituée qu’elle [les] a amassés, \q et ils retourneront au salaire d’une prostituée.
fr.B: Toutes ses idoles sculptées seront brisées en morceaux, tous les dons de ses temples brûlés au feu, \q et je dévasterai toutes ses images. \q Car elle les a amassés avec le salaire d’une prostituée, \q et ils redeviendront le salaire d’une prostituée.
fr.R: Toutes ses idoles seront brisées, et tous les cadeaux offerts dans ses sanctuaires seront brûlés. \q Je détruirai tous ses faux dieux. \q Elle les a obtenus comme une prostituée reçoit son salaire, \q et ils serviront de nouveau à payer des prostituées.

sw.L: Na sanamu zake zote za kuchonga zitavunjwa vipande vipande, na ujira wake wote utachomwa kwa moto, \q na sanamu zake zote nitazifanya ukiwa; \q kwa maana kutoka ujira wa kahaba alizikusanya, \q na kwa ujira wa kahaba zitarudi.
sw.B: Sanamu zake zote za kuchonga zitavunjwa vipande vipande, zawadi zote za mahekalu yake zitateketezwa motoni, \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitaziharibu sanamu zake zote. \q Kwa maana alizikusanya kutoka kwa malipo ya kahaba, \q nazo zitarudi kuwa malipo ya kahaba.
sw.R: Sanamu zake zote zitavunjwa, na zawadi zote zilizotolewa mahali pake pa ibada zitachomwa. \q Nitaziharibu miungu yake yote ya uongo. \q Alizipata kama kahaba anavyopata malipo yake, \q nazo zitatumika tena kuwalipa makahaba.

vi.L: Mọi tượng chạm của nó sẽ bị đập nát, mọi tiền công của nó sẽ bị lửa thiêu, \q và mọi thần tượng của nó {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho hoang tàn; \q vì nó đã thu góp [chúng] từ tiền công của gái điếm, \q và chúng sẽ trở lại làm tiền công của gái điếm.
vi.B: Mọi tượng chạm của nó sẽ bị đập nát, mọi lễ vật dâng tại các miếu của nó sẽ bị thiêu trong lửa, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ hủy phá mọi hình tượng của nó. \q Vì nó đã gom góp chúng bằng tiền công của gái điếm, \q và chúng sẽ trở thành tiền công của gái điếm.
vi.R: Mọi thần tượng của nó sẽ bị đập vỡ, mọi lễ vật dâng tại các miếu thờ của nó sẽ bị đốt cháy. \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ tiêu diệt mọi thần giả của nó. \q Nó đã có được những thứ ấy như gái điếm nhận tiền công, \q và chúng sẽ lại bị dùng để trả cho gái điếm.

ko.L: 그리고 그 성의 모든 새긴 우상이 부서지고, 그 모든 화대가 불에 탈 것이며, \q 내가 그 모든 우상을 황폐하게 만들 것이다. \q 그 성이 창녀의 화대로 [그것들을] 모았으니, \q 창녀의 화대로 돌아갈 것이다.
ko.B: 그 성의 새긴 우상들은 모두 산산조각이 나고, 신전에 바친 예물은 모두 불에 탈 것이다. \q 내가 그 성의 우상들을 모두 쓸어버리겠다. \q 그 성이 창녀의 몸값으로 그것들을 모았으니, \q 그것들이 다시 창녀의 몸값이 될 것이다.
ko.R: 그 성의 우상들이 모두 부서지고, 산꼭대기 제단에 바친 예물이 모두 불탈 것이다. \q 내가 그 성의 거짓 신들을 모두 없애 버리겠다. \q 그 성은 창녀가 몸값을 받듯이 그것들을 얻었으니, \q 그것들은 다시 창녀의 몸값으로 쓰일 것이다.

decisions.choice: wages of a prostitute: the gifts offered at the shrines, pictured as a prostitute's fee
decisions.reason: The word is the payment given to a prostitute (Deuteronomy 23:19). Hosea uses it of the grain and wine Israel thought its idols had given it (Hosea 2:14; 9:1). Here "her wages" stand beside her images and idols, so they are the gifts and valuables given at the shrines, perhaps the silver and gold the idols were overlaid with. Worshiping other gods is pictured as prostitution, unfaithfulness to the LORD.

decisions.choice: from a prostitute's wages ... to a prostitute's wages: what was gathered by unfaithfulness will be spent the same way
decisions.reason: The line turns on itself. Samaria built up her shrines with gifts gained in false worship; the enemy will carry them off, and they will again become offerings in a foreign temple, or pay for its prostitutes. Either way, what came from false worship goes back to it, and Samaria keeps nothing. The text does not say exactly how they will return.

decisions.choice: carved images ... idols: two words for the images of false gods
decisions.reason: The first word means an image carved from wood or stone, the second an idol of any kind, a word related to the word for pain or toil. Together with the shrine gifts they name everything Samaria's false worship had gathered.

decisions.choice: wages (L); temple gifts, a prostitute's pay (B); the gifts given at her shrines, the way a prostitute gets her pay (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one word, "wages", for all three uses so that the repetition shows. Balanced and Readable say what "her wages" were (m1), and keep the picture of a prostitute's pay in the second half.

decisions.choice: "ganancias" and "paga de prostituta" (L); "ofrendas de sus templos" (B); "los regalos que se dieron en sus santuarios" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one picture, a prostitute's earnings; Balanced and Readable say first what the "wages" were, gifts given at the shrines.

decisions.choice: "ujira" (L) for all three uses; "zawadi za mahekalu yake", "malipo ya kahaba" (B); "zawadi zilizotolewa mahali pake pa ibada" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one word so the repetition shows; Balanced and Readable say what her wages were (m1).

decisions.choice: "tiền công của gái điếm"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: the shrine gifts pictured as a prostitute's fee. The terms note keeps such texts plain, neither softened nor coarser than the Hebrew; "gái điếm" is plain without being vulgar.

decisions.choice: "화대" (L) for all three uses; "신전에 바친 예물", "창녀의 몸값" (B, R); "그 성" for Samaria
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one word so the repetition shows (m1). Korean avoids a feminine pronoun for the city and says "그 성", as Isaiah and Jeremiah do.

source.text: עַל־זֹאת֙ אֶסְפְּדָ֣ה וְאֵילִ֔ילָה אֵילְכָ֥ה שׁוֹלָ֖ל וְעָר֑וֹם אֶעֱשֶׂ֤ה מִסְפֵּד֙ כַּתַּנִּ֔ים וְאֵ֖בֶל כִּבְנ֥וֹת יַעֲנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: On this I will lament and I will wail; I will go barefoot and naked; I will make a lament like jackals and a mourning like [the] daughters of an ostrich.

en.L: Because of this I will lament and wail; \q I will go barefoot and naked; \q I will make a lament like the jackals \q and mourning like the ostriches.
en.B: For this I will mourn and wail; \q I will go about barefoot and stripped. \q I will howl like the jackals \q and mourn like the ostriches.
en.R: Because of this I will mourn and cry aloud. \q I will walk around barefoot and stripped of my clothes. \q I will howl like a jackal \q and cry like an ostrich.

es.L: Por esto me lamentaré y gemiré; \q andaré descalzo y desnudo; \q haré lamento como los chacales \q y duelo como los avestruces.
es.B: Por esto haré duelo y gemiré; \q andaré descalzo y despojado. \q Aullaré como los chacales \q y me lamentaré como los avestruces.
es.R: Por esto lloraré y gritaré de dolor. \q Andaré descalzo y sin ropa. \q Aullaré como un chacal \q y gritaré como un avestruz.

fr.L: À cause de cela je me lamenterai et je hurlerai ; \q j’irai déchaussé et nu ; \q je ferai une lamentation comme les chacals \q et un deuil comme les autruches.
fr.B: Voilà pourquoi je vais pleurer et gémir ; \q j’irai pieds nus et dépouillé. \q Je hurlerai comme les chacals \q et je me lamenterai comme les autruches.
fr.R: À cause de cela, je vais pleurer et crier fort. \q Je marcherai pieds nus, sans vêtements. \q Je hurlerai comme un chacal \q et je crierai comme une autruche.

sw.L: Kwa sababu ya hili nitaomboleza na kulia kwa uchungu; \q nitatembea bila viatu na uchi; \q nitaomboleza kama mbweha \q na kulia kama mbuni.
sw.B: Kwa ajili ya hili nitaomboleza na kupiga yowe; \q nitazunguka bila viatu na bila nguo. \q Nitalia kama mbweha \q na kuomboleza kama mbuni.
sw.R: Kwa sababu ya hili nitaomboleza na kulia kwa sauti. \q Nitatembea bila viatu na bila nguo zangu. \q Nitalia kama mbweha \q na kupiga kelele kama mbuni.

vi.L: Vì điều này tôi sẽ than khóc và kêu gào; \q tôi sẽ đi chân không và trần truồng; \q tôi sẽ cất tiếng than như chó rừng \q và kêu thương như đà điểu.
vi.B: Vì thế tôi sẽ khóc than và kêu gào; \q tôi sẽ đi chân không, mình trần. \q Tôi sẽ tru lên như chó rừng \q và rên rỉ như đà điểu.
vi.R: Vì điều này tôi sẽ khóc than và kêu lớn tiếng. \q Tôi sẽ đi chân không và cởi bỏ quần áo. \q Tôi sẽ tru lên như chó rừng \q và kêu khóc như đà điểu.

ko.L: 이 때문에 내가 슬퍼하며 울부짖을 것이다. \q 맨발과 벌거숭이로 다닐 것이다. \q 승냥이들처럼 애곡하고 \q 타조들처럼 슬피 울 것이다.
ko.B: 이 때문에 내가 슬퍼하며 통곡하겠다. \q 맨발에 옷을 벗은 채로 다니겠다. \q 승냥이처럼 울부짖고 \q 타조처럼 슬피 울겠다.
ko.R: 이 일 때문에 나는 슬퍼하며 크게 울 것이다. \q 맨발로, 옷도 걸치지 않고 다닐 것이다. \q 승냥이처럼 울부짖고 \q 타조처럼 울 것이다.

decisions.choice: I will lament: the prophet himself now speaks
decisions.reason: The grief is the prophet's. He mourns over the judgment he has announced, which has now reached his own people (verse 9). Jeremiah grieves in the same way (Jeremiah 4:19; 8:21).

decisions.choice: barefoot and naked: stripped like a mourner or a captive
decisions.reason: Mourners went barefoot (2 Samuel 15:30), and prisoners of war were led away barefoot and stripped (Isaiah 20:2-4, where Isaiah walks "naked and barefoot" as a sign of the captivity to come). "Naked" means without the outer garment, wearing only what was underneath. The first word is spelled one way in the written text and read another way, as noted in the margin; the reading means barefoot or stripped (Job 12:17, 19).

decisions.choice: jackals ... ostriches: creatures of the wilderness, known for their cries
decisions.reason: Jackals howl at night, and the ostrich makes a loud, mournful call. Both live in deserted places and belong to pictures of ruin (Isaiah 13:21-22; Job 30:29). The Hebrew says "daughters of the ostrich", a common way of naming the bird; some take it to be an owl.

decisions.choice: naked (L); stripped (B); stripped of my clothes (R); like the ostriches
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "naked"; Balanced and Readable say "stripped", which is what the word means here (m2). The "daughters of the ostrich" are simply ostriches, as the expression means.

decisions.choice: the prophet speaks as "tôi"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: Micah himself now speaks. The terms note: a prophet speaking in his own voice says "tôi".

source.text: כִּ֥י אֲנוּשָׁ֖ה מַכּוֹתֶ֑יהָ כִּי־בָ֨אָה֙ עַד־יְהוּדָ֔ה נָגַ֛ע עַד־שַׁ֥עַר עַמִּ֖י עַד־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For incurable [are] her wounds; for it has come to Judah; it has reached to [the] gate of my people, to Jerusalem.

en.L: For her wounds [are] incurable, \q for it has come to Judah; \q it has reached to the gate of my people, to Jerusalem.
en.B: For her wound cannot be healed; \q it has spread to Judah. \q It has reached the gate of my people, Jerusalem itself.
en.R: Samaria's wound cannot be healed. \q The disaster has spread to Judah. \q It has reached Jerusalem, the gate where my people live.

es.L: Porque sus heridas [son] incurables, \q porque ha llegado hasta Judá; \q ha alcanzado hasta la puerta de mi pueblo, hasta Jerusalén.
es.B: Porque su herida no tiene cura; \q se ha extendido hasta Judá. \q Ha llegado a la puerta de mi pueblo, a Jerusalén misma.
es.R: La herida de Samaria no tiene cura. \q El desastre se ha extendido hasta Judá. \q Ha llegado a Jerusalén, la puerta donde vive mi pueblo.

fr.L: Car ses plaies [sont] incurables, \q car cela est venu jusqu’à Juda ; \q cela a atteint jusqu’à la porte de mon peuple, jusqu’à Jérusalem.
fr.B: Car sa blessure est inguérissable ; \q elle s’est étendue jusqu’à Juda. \q Elle a atteint la porte de mon peuple, Jérusalem elle-même.
fr.R: La blessure de Samarie ne peut pas guérir. \q Le malheur s’est étendu jusqu’à Juda. \q Il a atteint Jérusalem, la porte où vit mon peuple.

sw.L: Kwa maana majeraha yake [ni] yasiyoponyeka, \q kwa maana [pigo] limefika hata Yuda; \q limefika hata lango la watu wangu, hata Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Kwa maana jeraha lake haliponyeki; \q limeenea hadi Yuda. \q Limefika langoni pa watu wangu, Yerusalemu yenyewe.
sw.R: Jeraha la Samaria haliwezi kupona. \q Maafa yameenea hadi Yuda. \q Yamefika Yerusalemu, lango wanakoishi watu wangu.

vi.L: Vì các vết thương của nó [là] không thể chữa lành, \q vì nó đã đến Giu-đa; \q nó đã chạm đến cổng của dân tôi, đến Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: Vì vết thương của nó không thể chữa lành; \q tai họa đã lan đến Giu-đa. \q Nó đã đến tận cổng thành của dân tôi, chính Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Vết thương của Sa-ma-ri không thể chữa lành. \q Tai họa đã lan đến Giu-đa. \q Nó đã đến tận Giê-ru-sa-lem, cổng thành nơi dân tôi sinh sống.

ko.L: 그 상처들은 고칠 수 없으니, \q 그것이 유다에까지 이르렀고, \q 내 백성의 성문, 곧 예루살렘에까지 닿았기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그 상처는 나을 수 없다. \q 그것이 유다에까지 번졌다. \q 내 백성의 성문, 바로 예루살렘에까지 이르렀다.
ko.R: 사마리아의 상처는 나을 수 없다. \q 그 재앙이 유다에까지 번졌다. \q 내 백성이 사는 성문, 예루살렘에까지 이르렀다.

decisions.choice: her wounds are incurable ... it has come: Samaria's death blow spreads south to Judah
decisions.reason: "Her" is Samaria (verse 6). The noun is plural but the word "incurable" is singular, as if the blows were one wound; the verb "it has come" also has the wound, or the disaster, as its subject. The judgment that falls on Samaria will not stop at the border.

decisions.choice: the gate of my people: Jerusalem, the city where Judah gathers
decisions.reason: A city's gate was where its people met, traded and held court; to reach the gate is to reach the city itself. The prophet calls Judah "my people", his own. Assyria's army did reach Jerusalem in 701 BC but did not take it (2 Kings 18:13-19:36).

decisions.choice: her wound (B); Samaria's wound, The disaster (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "wound" in the singular, as the grammar treats it (m1). Readable names Samaria and says what has spread.

source.text: בְּגַת֙ אַל־תַּגִּ֔ידוּ בָּכ֖וֹ אַל־תִּבְכּ֑וּ בְּבֵ֣ית לְעַפְרָ֔ה עָפָ֖ר הִתְפַּלָּֽשִׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: In Gath do not tell; weeping, do not weep; in Beth-leaphrah in dust roll yourself.

en.L: Do not tell [it] in Gath; \q do not weep at all. \q In Beth-leaphrah roll yourself in [the] dust.
en.B: Do not tell it in Gath; \q do not weep at all. \q In Beth-leaphrah, roll in the dust.
en.R: Do not tell the news in Gath. \q Do not let your enemies see you cry. \q In Beth-leaphrah, the House of Dust, roll in the dust to show your sorrow.

es.L: No lo {{plural_you:anuncien|anunciéis}} en Gat; \q no {{plural_you:lloren|lloréis}} en absoluto. \q En Bet-le-afrá revuélcate en [el] polvo.
es.B: No lo {{plural_you:cuenten|contéis}} en Gat; \q no {{plural_you:lloren|lloréis}} en absoluto. \q En Bet-le-afrá, revuélcate en el polvo.
es.R: No {{plural_you:den|deis}} la noticia en Gat. \q No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} enemigos {{plural_you:los|os}} vean llorar. \q En Bet-le-afrá, la Casa del Polvo, revuélcate en el polvo para mostrar tu dolor.

fr.L: À Gath, ne [l’]annoncez pas ; \q ne pleurez surtout pas. \q À Beth-Leaphra, roule-toi dans [la] poussière.
fr.B: Ne l’annoncez pas à Gath ; \q ne pleurez surtout pas. \q À Beth-Leaphra, roule-toi dans la poussière.
fr.R: N’annoncez pas la nouvelle à Gath. \q Ne laissez pas vos ennemis vous voir pleurer. \q À Beth-Leaphra, la Maison-de-Poussière, roule-toi dans la poussière pour montrer ta tristesse.

sw.L: Msiseme [hivyo] katika Gathi; \q msilie kabisa. \q Huko Beth-leafra jigaragaze katika mavumbi.
sw.B: Msiseme jambo hili katika Gathi; \q msilie kabisa. \q Huko Beth-leafra, gaagaa mavumbini.
sw.R: Msiipeleke habari hii Gathi. \q Msiwaache adui zenu wawaone mkilia. \q Huko Beth-leafra, yaani Nyumba ya Mavumbi, gaagaa mavumbini kuonyesha huzuni yako.

vi.L: Chớ báo [tin] tại Gát; \q chớ khóc lóc gì cả. \q Tại Bết-Lê-áp-ra hãy lăn mình trong bụi đất.
vi.B: Đừng loan tin ấy tại Gát; \q đừng khóc lóc chi cả. \q Tại Bết-Lê-áp-ra, hãy lăn mình trong bụi đất.
vi.R: Đừng báo tin này tại Gát. \q Đừng để kẻ thù thấy các ngươi khóc. \q Tại Bết-Lê-áp-ra, nghĩa là Nhà Bụi Đất, hãy lăn mình trong bụi đất để tỏ nỗi buồn.

ko.L: 가드에 [그것을] 알리지 마라. \q 결코 울지 마라. \q 베들레아브라에서 티끌 속에 뒹굴어라.
ko.B: 가드에 이 일을 알리지 마라. \q 조금도 울지 마라. \q 베들레아브라에서 티끌에 뒹굴어라.
ko.R: 가드에 이 소식을 전하지 마라. \q 원수들이 너희가 우는 것을 보지 못하게 하여라. \q '티끌의 집'이라는 뜻의 베들레아브라에서 티끌에 뒹굴며 슬픔을 나타내어라.

decisions.choice: Do not tell it in Gath: the words of David's lament for Saul and Jonathan
decisions.reason: David began his lament with "Do not tell it in Gath" (2 Samuel 1:20), so that the Philistines would not gloat over Israel's defeat. Micah takes up the line as he begins to mourn over the towns of his own district. In Hebrew the name Gath sounds like the verb "tell", the first of the wordplays on place names that run through verses 10-15.

decisions.choice: do not weep at all: as the Hebrew text reads
decisions.reason: The Hebrew doubles the verb for emphasis, "weeping, do not weep". Since every other line in these verses names a town, some read the first word as a place name, "in Acco" or "in Bochim" (the ancient Greek translation has a name here). The Hebrew as it stands makes sense, so it is kept.

decisions.choice: Beth-leaphrah: "house of dust", where the people roll in the dust
decisions.reason: The name means "house of dust" or "house of the fawn", and the line plays on it: the people of Dust-town must roll in the dust, a sign of mourning (Jeremiah 6:26; Ezekiel 27:30). Its site is not known.

decisions.choice: roll yourself: the reading noted in the margin
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has "I have rolled myself"; the scribes noted in the margin that it is read "roll yourself", addressed to the town as a woman. The command fits the commands around it, and the margin's reading is followed.

decisions.choice: Do not let your enemies see you cry; the House of Dust; to show your sorrow (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says why there is to be no weeping in Gath, the Philistines' city (m1), gives the meaning of Beth-leaphrah so that the wordplay can be heard (m3), and says what rolling in the dust meant. These additions explain; they do not change what is said.

decisions.choice: "No lo anuncien en Gat" (L); "No lo cuenten en Gat" (B); "No den la noticia en Gat" (R)
decisions.reason: The line quotes David's lament, so each level reuses the published Spanish of 2 Samuel 1:20, with its plural_you spans.

decisions.choice: town names "Bet-le-afrá", "Safir", "Zaanán", "Bet-ézel", "Marot", "Moréset-gat", "Maresa"; Readable gives each pun as an added name: "la Casa del Polvo", "la Ciudad Hermosa", "la Ciudad de la Salida", "la Ciudad Amarga", "la Ciudad del Engaño"
decisions.reason: Names not yet published are spelled on the pattern of published ones (Bet-togarma, Moréset, Laquis, Aczib, Adulam). The English Readable explains the wordplay the same way.

decisions.choice: "Ne l'annoncez pas à Gath" (B), "N'annoncez pas la nouvelle à Gath" (R), the published 2 Samuel 1:20
decisions.reason: Micah takes up David's lament for Saul, as the English meaning decision notes; French reuses its published words.

decisions.choice: Readable gives the meanings of the town names as hyphenated French names ("la Maison-de-Poussière", "la Belle-Ville", "la Ville-de-la-Sortie", "la Ville-Amère", "la Ville-du-Mensonge") where the English Readable adds them; the names themselves keep the English form with French spelling (Beth-Leaphra, Shaphir, Tsaanân, Beth-Étsel, Maroth, Lakish, Morèsheth-Gath, Akzib, Marésha, Adoullam)
alternatives: explaining the names in footnotes only
decisions.reason: The wordplay on the town names is the point of 1:10-15; Readable lets a reader hear it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Msiseme [hivyo] katika Gathi" (L); "Msiseme jambo hili katika Gathi" (B)
decisions.reason: Each level reuses the published Swahili 2 Samuel 1:20, the line of David's lament that Micah takes up (m1).

decisions.choice: town names "Beth-leafra", "Shafiri", "Saanani", "Beth-eseli", "Marothi", "Lakishi", "Moresheth-gathi", "Akzibu", "Maresha", "Adulamu"; Readable gives each pun as a name: "Nyumba ya Mavumbi", "Mji Mzuri", "Mji wa Kutoka", "Mji Mchungu", "Mji wa Uongo"
decisions.reason: Names already published (Gathi, Lakishi, Akzibu, Maresha, Adulamu) keep their Joshua forms; the others follow the usual Swahili pattern. Readable lets the wordplays be heard where the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Chớ báo [tin] tại Gát" (L); "Đừng loan tin ấy tại Gát" (B)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision names David's lament in 2 Samuel 1:20; the line follows the sense of the published Vietnamese there without copying its whole sentence. Readable explains the place names as the English Readable does ("nghĩa là Nhà Bụi Đất"), here and in verses 11-15.

decisions.choice: "가드에 [그것을] 알리지 마라" (L), "가드에 이 일을 알리지 마라" (B), as 2 Samuel 1:20; town names "베들레아브라", "사빌", "사아난", "벧에셀", "마롯", "라기스", "모레셋가드", "악십", "마레사", "아둘람"
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced reuse the published Korean 2 Samuel 1:20 (m1). Names published in Joshua keep their forms; Readable gives the meaning of a name in quotation marks where the English Readable adds it.

source.text: עִבְרִ֥י לָכֶ֛ם יוֹשֶׁ֥בֶת שָׁפִ֖יר עֶרְיָה־בֹ֑שֶׁת לֹ֤א יָֽצְאָה֙ יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת צַֽאֲנָ֔ן מִסְפַּד֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֵ֔צֶל יִקַּ֥ח מִכֶּ֖ם עֶמְדָּתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Pass on for yourselves, inhabitant of Shaphir, [in] nakedness [and] shame; not has come out [the] inhabitant of Zaanan; [the] lament of Beth-ezel will take from you its standing place.

en.L: Pass on for yourselves, inhabitant of Shaphir, in nakedness [and] shame; \q the inhabitant of Zaanan has not come out; \q the lament of Beth-ezel— \q it will take from you its standing place.
en.B: Pass on your way, people of Shaphir, in shameful nakedness. \q The people of Zaanan have not come out. \q Beth-ezel is mourning; \q it will take its support away from you.
en.R: People of Shaphir, the Lovely Town, go away into exile, naked and ashamed. \q The people of Zaanan, the Going-Out Town, do not dare to go out. \q Beth-ezel is weeping, \q and it can give you no shelter.

es.L: Pasa de largo, tú que habitas en Safir, en desnudez [y] vergüenza; \q no ha salido la que habita en Zaanán; \q el lamento de Bet-ézel— \q {{plural_you:les|os}} quitará su lugar de apoyo.
es.B: Sigue tu camino, gente de Safir, desnuda y avergonzada. \q La gente de Zaanán no ha salido. \q Bet-ézel está de luto; \q {{plural_you:les|os}} quitará su apoyo.
es.R: Gente de Safir, la Ciudad Hermosa, vete al destierro desnuda y avergonzada. \q La gente de Zaanán, la Ciudad de la Salida, no se atreve a salir. \q Bet-ézel está llorando, \q y no {{plural_you:les|os}} puede dar refugio.

fr.L: Passe, pour vous, habitante de Shaphir, dans la nudité [et] la honte ; \q l’habitante de Tsaanân n’est pas sortie ; \q la lamentation de Beth-Étsel… \q elle vous ôtera son lieu d’appui.
fr.B: Passe ton chemin, population de Shaphir, dans une honteuse nudité. \q La population de Tsaanân n’est pas sortie. \q Beth-Étsel est en deuil ; \q elle vous retire son soutien.
fr.R: Shaphir, la Belle-Ville, pars en exil, nue et couverte de honte. \q Tsaanân, la Ville-de-la-Sortie, n’ose pas sortir. \q Beth-Étsel pleure, \q et elle ne peut plus vous protéger.

sw.L: Pita, ewe mkaaji wa Shafiri, katika uchi [na] aibu; \q mkaaji wa Saanani hakutoka; \q maombolezo ya Beth-eseli— \q yatawaondolea mahali pake pa kusimama.
sw.B: Piteni mwende zenu, enyi watu wa Shafiri, katika uchi wa aibu. \q Watu wa Saanani hawajatoka nje. \q Beth-eseli inaomboleza; \q itawaondolea msaada wake.
sw.R: Enyi watu wa Shafiri, Mji Mzuri, nendeni uhamishoni mkiwa uchi na wenye aibu. \q Watu wa Saanani, Mji wa Kutoka, hawathubutu kutoka nje. \q Beth-eseli inalia, \q wala haiwezi kuwapa makazi.

vi.L: Hãy đi qua, hỡi dân cư Sa-phia, trong sự trần truồng [và] xấu hổ; \q dân cư Xa-a-nan không dám ra; \q tiếng than khóc của Bết-Ê-xên— \q nó sẽ lấy khỏi các ngươi chỗ đứng của nó.
vi.B: Hãy đi đi, hỡi dân Sa-phia, trần truồng và nhục nhã. \q Dân Xa-a-nan không dám ra ngoài. \q Bết-Ê-xên đang than khóc; \q nó sẽ rút lại chỗ nương tựa khỏi các ngươi.
vi.R: Hỡi dân Sa-phia, Thành Xinh Đẹp, hãy đi lưu đày, trần truồng và xấu hổ. \q Dân Xa-a-nan, Thành Đi Ra, không dám đi ra. \q Bết-Ê-xên đang khóc than, \q và chẳng thể che chở các ngươi.

ko.L: 사빌의 주민아, 벌거벗은 수치 가운데 너희는 지나가라. \q 사아난의 주민은 나오지 못했다. \q 벧에셀의 애곡이— \q 너희에게서 그 설 곳을 빼앗을 것이다.
ko.B: 사빌 사람들아, 부끄러운 알몸으로 지나가거라. \q 사아난 사람들은 나오지 못했다. \q 벧에셀이 슬피 울고 있으니, \q 너희에게 의지할 곳이 되어 주지 못할 것이다.
ko.R: '아름다운 마을' 사빌 사람들아, 벌거벗고 부끄러운 모습으로 포로가 되어 끌려가거라. \q '나가는 마을' 사아난 사람들은 감히 밖으로 나가지 못한다. \q 벧에셀이 울고 있으니, \q 너희를 숨겨 줄 수 없다.

decisions.choice: Shaphir, Zaanan, Beth-ezel: the names play against what will happen to the towns
decisions.reason: Shaphir means "beautiful" or "pleasant", and its people will go out naked and ashamed. Zaanan sounds like the verb "come out", and its people will not come out, perhaps for fear of the enemy outside the walls. Beth-ezel may mean "house beside" or "house of nearness", and it will give no support to those who lean on it. The meaning of the names and the plays on them are not all certain.

decisions.choice: the lament of Beth-ezel will take from you its standing place: a line whose sense is not clear
alternatives: the mourning of Beth-ezel will take away its support from you
the enemy will take his stand from Beth-ezel against you
decisions.reason: The words are clear but how they fit together is not. The last word means a place to stand, and so a position or support. The line seems to say that Beth-ezel, itself in mourning, can give no help, or that the enemy will take Beth-ezel as a base. The first sense is followed here.

decisions.choice: pass on: go into exile; the towns are in the low hills near Micah's home
decisions.reason: "Pass on" means go away, probably as captives. The towns of verses 10-15 lie in the low hill country west and southwest of Jerusalem, around Micah's town of Moresheth: Gath, Lachish, Mareshah, Achzib and Adullam are known sites; Shaphir, Zaanan, Beth-ezel, Beth-leaphrah and Maroth are not. They lay on the road an army from the coast would take toward Jerusalem, as Sennacherib's army did in 701 BC.

decisions.choice: inhabitant: the people of a town, spoken of as one woman
decisions.reason: The word is a feminine singular, "she who lives in", used for the whole population of a town personified as a woman (Isaiah 12:6; Jeremiah 46:19).

decisions.choice: people of (B, R); the Lovely Town, the Going-Out Town, go away into exile, do not dare, can give you no shelter (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "people of" for "inhabitant of" (m4). Readable gives the meaning of the names so that the wordplays can be heard (m1), says what "pass on" means (m3), and gives the sense chosen for the hard last line (m2).

decisions.choice: "tú que habitas en", "la que habita en" (L); "gente de" with feminine agreement (B, R)
decisions.reason: Each town's people are spoken of as one woman; Spanish keeps the singular and the feminine, as the term sheet does for cities addressed as women.

decisions.choice: "habitante" (L), "population" (B), the town's own name (R), with feminine agreement and "tu": each town is spoken to as one woman
decisions.reason: The Hebrew addresses each town as a woman in the singular; French "population" is feminine and singular, so Balanced can say "people of" as the English does and still keep the Hebrew's number and gender.

decisions.choice: "mkaaji wa" (L); "watu wa" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of each town's people as one woman (m4). Swahili verbs show no gender, so Literal keeps the singular "mkaaji" and Balanced and Readable say "watu wa", as the English does.

decisions.choice: the town names "Sa-phia", "Xa-a-nan", "Bết-Ê-xên" (and "Ma-rốt", "Bết-Lê-áp-ra", "Mô-rê-sết-Gát" in the next verses)
decisions.reason: New transliterations in the Protestant pattern. Zaanan may be the Zenan of Joshua 15:37 ("Xê-nan"), but the Hebrew spelling differs and the play on "go out" needs this form. Published forms are kept for La-ki, Ạc-xíp, Ma-rê-sa and A-đu-lam.

source.text: כִּֽי־חָ֥לָֽה לְט֖וֹב יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת מָר֑וֹת כִּֽי־יָ֤רַד רָע֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה לְשַׁ֖עַר יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For writhes for good [the] inhabitant of Maroth, for has come down calamity from Yahweh to [the] gate of Jerusalem.

en.L: For the inhabitant of Maroth writhes, [waiting] for good, \q for disaster has come down from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q to the gate of Jerusalem.
en.B: The people of Maroth writhe in pain as they wait for relief, \q for disaster has come down from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q to the very gate of Jerusalem.
en.R: The people of Maroth, the Bitter Town, long for something good to happen. \q But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent disaster down \q to the gates of Jerusalem.

es.L: Porque la que habita en Marot se retuerce [esperando] el bien, \q porque ha descendido el desastre de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} \q hasta la puerta de Jerusalén.
es.B: La gente de Marot se retuerce de dolor esperando alivio, \q porque el desastre ha descendido de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} \q hasta la misma puerta de Jerusalén.
es.R: La gente de Marot, la Ciudad Amarga, anhela que pase algo bueno. \q Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha enviado el desastre \q hasta las puertas de Jerusalén.

fr.L: Car l’habitante de Maroth se tord [dans l’attente] du bien, \q car le malheur est descendu de la part {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} \q jusqu’à la porte de Jérusalem.
fr.B: La population de Maroth se tord de douleur en attendant un soulagement, \q car le malheur est descendu de la part {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} \q jusqu’à la porte même de Jérusalem.
fr.R: Maroth, la Ville-Amère, espère que quelque chose de bon lui arrivera. \q Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait descendre le malheur \q jusqu’aux portes de Jérusalem.

sw.L: Kwa maana mkaaji wa Marothi anateseka kwa maumivu, [akingojea] mema, \q kwa maana mabaya yameshuka kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} \q hadi lango la Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Watu wa Marothi wanateseka kwa maumivu wakingojea nafuu, \q kwa maana maafa yameshuka kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} \q hadi kwenye lango lenyewe la Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Watu wa Marothi, Mji Mchungu, wanatamani jambo jema litokee. \q Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameshusha maafa \q hadi kwenye malango ya Yerusalemu.

vi.L: Vì dân cư Ma-rốt quằn quại, [chờ] điều tốt lành, \q vì tai họa đã từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giáng xuống \q đến cổng Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: Dân Ma-rốt quằn quại đau đớn chờ ngày được cứu, \q vì tai họa từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giáng xuống \q đến tận cổng Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Dân Ma-rốt, Thành Cay Đắng, mong mỏi điều tốt lành xảy đến. \q Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giáng tai họa xuống \q đến tận các cổng Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: 마롯의 주민이 좋은 것을 [기다리며] 몸부림친다. \q 재앙이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께로부터 \q 예루살렘 성문에까지 내려왔기 때문이다.
ko.B: 마롯 사람들이 구원을 기다리며 고통으로 몸부림친다. \q 재앙이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께로부터 \q 예루살렘 성문 바로 앞까지 내려왔기 때문이다.
ko.R: '쓴 마을' 마롯 사람들은 좋은 일이 일어나기를 애타게 기다린다. \q 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 재앙을 내려 보내셔서 \q 예루살렘 성문들에까지 이르게 하셨다.

decisions.choice: Maroth: a name meaning "bitterness", set against "good"
decisions.reason: The town's name means "bitter things". Its people hope for good, but what comes is bitter. The site is not known; it may be the Maarath of Joshua 15:59.

decisions.choice: writhes for good: waits in anguish for relief that does not come
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to writhe in pain, as a woman in labor. With "for good" it seems to mean waiting anxiously for good news or help; a related verb means to wait. Either way the people are in distress and the help they hope for is not coming.

decisions.choice: disaster has come down from the LORD: the invasion is the LORD's judgment
decisions.reason: The enemy's army is the agent; the LORD is the one who sends it, as Amos 3:6 asks: "Does disaster come to a city unless the LORD has done it?" The word "disaster" is the common word for evil, here meaning harm. The same disaster that struck Samaria reaches Jerusalem's gate (verse 9).

decisions.choice: [waiting] for good (L); as they wait for relief (B); the Bitter Town, long for something good to happen (R)
decisions.reason: The levels give the sense of the hard phrase "writhes for good" (m2). Readable gives the meaning of Maroth so that the wordplay can be heard.

source.text: רְתֹ֧ם הַמֶּרְכָּבָ֛ה לָרֶ֖כֶשׁ יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת לָכִ֑ישׁ רֵאשִׁ֨ית חַטָּ֥את הִיא֙ לְבַת־צִיּ֔וֹן כִּי־בָ֥ךְ נִמְצְא֖וּ פִּשְׁעֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Harness the chariot to the steed[s], inhabitant of Lachish; [the] beginning of sin [was] she for [the] daughter of Zion, for in you were found [the] transgressions of Israel.

en.L: Harness the chariot to the steeds, inhabitant of Lachish; \q she [was] the beginning of sin for the daughter of Zion, \q for in you were found the transgressions of Israel.
en.B: Harness the horses to the chariot, people of Lachish! \q You were the beginning of sin for Daughter Zion, \q for the rebellious ways of Israel were found in you.
en.R: People of Lachish, hitch your fastest horses to your chariots and flee! \q You were the first to lead the people of Zion into sin, \q because you copied the sins of Israel.

es.L: Ata el carro a los corceles, tú que habitas en Laquis; \q ella [fue] el principio del pecado para la hija de Sion, \q porque en ti se hallaron las transgresiones de Israel.
es.B: ¡Engancha los caballos al carro, gente de Laquis! \q Tú fuiste el principio del pecado para la hija de Sion, \q porque en ti se hallaron los delitos de Israel.
es.R: Gente de Laquis, ¡engancha tus caballos más veloces a tus carros y huye! \q Tú fuiste la primera en llevar al pueblo de Sion al pecado, \q porque copiaste los pecados de Israel.

fr.L: Attelle le char aux coursiers, habitante de Lakish ; \q elle [fut] le commencement du péché pour la fille de Sion, \q car en toi ont été trouvées les transgressions d’Israël.
fr.B: Attelle les chevaux au char, population de Lakish ! \q Tu as été le commencement du péché pour la fille de Sion, \q car c’est chez toi qu’on a trouvé les rébellions d’Israël.
fr.R: Lakish, attelle tes chevaux les plus rapides à tes chars et fuis ! \q Tu as été la première à entraîner le peuple de Sion dans le péché, \q car tu as imité les péchés d’Israël.

sw.L: Funga gari la vita kwa farasi wepesi, ewe mkaaji wa Lakishi; \q yeye [alikuwa] mwanzo wa dhambi kwa binti Sayuni, \q kwa maana ndani yako yalionekana maasi ya Israeli.
sw.B: Fungeni farasi kwenye magari ya vita, enyi watu wa Lakishi! \q Mlikuwa mwanzo wa dhambi kwa Binti Sayuni, \q kwa maana makosa ya Israeli yalionekana kwenu.
sw.R: Enyi watu wa Lakishi, fungeni farasi wenu wepesi kabisa kwenye magari yenu mkimbie! \q Ninyi mlikuwa wa kwanza kuwaongoza watu wa Sayuni katika dhambi, \q kwa sababu mliiga dhambi za Israeli.

vi.L: Hãy thắng xe vào ngựa chiến, hỡi dân cư La-ki; \q nó [là] khởi đầu tội lỗi cho con gái Si-ôn, \q vì nơi ngươi đã tìm thấy các tội vi phạm của Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Hỡi dân La-ki, hãy thắng ngựa vào xe! \q Ngươi là khởi đầu tội lỗi cho con gái Si-ôn, \q vì những tội ác của Y-sơ-ra-ên đã được thấy nơi ngươi.
vi.R: Hỡi dân La-ki, hãy thắng những con ngựa nhanh nhất vào xe mà chạy trốn! \q Các ngươi là những người đầu tiên dẫn dân Si-ôn vào tội lỗi, \q vì các ngươi đã bắt chước tội lỗi của Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 라기스의 주민아, 병거를 준마에 매어라. \q 그 성은 딸 시온에게 죄의 시작이었다. \q 이스라엘의 반역들이 네 안에서 발견되었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 라기스 주민아, 말들을 병거에 매어라! \q 너는 딸 시온에게 죄의 시작이었다. \q 이스라엘의 반역이 네 안에서 드러났기 때문이다.
ko.R: 라기스 사람들아, 가장 빠른 말들을 병거에 매고 도망쳐라! \q 너희가 맨 처음 시온 백성을 죄에 빠뜨렸다. \q 너희가 이스라엘의 죄를 본받았기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: Lachish and the steeds: a play on sound
decisions.reason: The word for steeds, fast horses for chariots, sounds like the name Lachish. Lachish was the strongest fortress city of the low hills, a city of chariots and horses. Sennacherib besieged and took it in 701 BC (2 Kings 18:14, 17), and his palace reliefs at Nineveh show the siege. The command to harness the horses is a call to flee.

decisions.choice: the beginning of sin for the daughter of Zion: Lachish led Jerusalem into Israel's sins
decisions.reason: The text does not say what Lachish's sin was. Its trust in horses and chariots may be meant, which the prophets condemn (Isaiah 31:1; Hosea 14:4; compare Deuteronomy 17:16), or a shrine where the worship of the north was copied. "The daughter of Zion" is Jerusalem and its people, spoken of as a young woman.

decisions.choice: she ... you: the line turns from speaking about Lachish to speaking to her
decisions.reason: Hebrew poetry often moves between "she" and "you" for the same person. Here Lachish is first addressed, then spoken about, then addressed again.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Zion (L); Daughter Zion (B); the people of Zion (R); transgressions (L); rebellious ways (B); sins (R); You were (B, R)
decisions.reason: The forms for the daughter of Zion and for transgression follow the wording set for the prophets. Balanced and Readable say "you" throughout, since Lachish is addressed. Readable says what harnessing the horses was for (m1).

decisions.choice: "la hija de Sion" (L, B); "el pueblo de Sion" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled Spanish for "daughter Zion" (Isaiah, Matthew 21:5).

decisions.choice: "la fille de Sion" (L, B), "le peuple de Sion" (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet and published Isaiah.

decisions.choice: "binti Sayuni" (L); "Binti Sayuni" (B); "watu wa Sayuni" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled forms for Daughter Zion in the prophets, as 2 Kings 19:21.

decisions.choice: "딸 시온" (L, B); "시온 백성" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled forms for Daughter Zion, as 2 Kings 19:21.

source.text: לָכֵן֙ תִּתְּנִ֣י שִׁלּוּחִ֔ים עַ֖ל מוֹרֶ֣שֶׁת גַּ֑ת בָּתֵּ֤י אַכְזִיב֙ לְאַכְזָ֔ב לְמַלְכֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore you will give parting gifts to Moresheth-gath; [the] houses of Achzib [will be] a deception to [the] kings of Israel.

en.L: Therefore you will give parting gifts \q to Moresheth-gath; \q the houses of Achzib [will be] a deception \q to the kings of Israel.
en.B: So you will give farewell gifts \q to Moresheth-gath. \q The houses of Achzib will prove a deception \q to the kings of Israel.
en.R: So you must say goodbye to Moresheth-gath \q and give her parting gifts, as a father does for a daughter who marries and leaves home. \q Achzib, the Town of Lies, \q will let the kings of Israel down.

es.L: Por tanto, darás regalos de despedida \q a Moréset-gat; \q las casas de Aczib [serán] un engaño \q para los reyes de Israel.
es.B: Por eso darás regalos de despedida \q a Moréset-gat. \q Las casas de Aczib resultarán un engaño \q para los reyes de Israel.
es.R: Por eso tendrás que despedirte de Moréset-gat \q y darle regalos de despedida, como hace un padre con una hija que se casa y deja su casa. \q Aczib, la Ciudad del Engaño, \q les fallará a los reyes de Israel.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi tu donneras des présents d’adieu \q à Morèsheth-Gath ; \q les maisons d’Akzib [seront] une tromperie \q pour les rois d’Israël.
fr.B: Aussi donneras-tu des cadeaux d’adieu \q à Morèsheth-Gath. \q Les maisons d’Akzib se révéleront trompeuses \q pour les rois d’Israël.
fr.R: Alors tu devras dire au revoir à Morèsheth-Gath \q et lui donner des cadeaux d’adieu, comme un père à sa fille qui se marie et quitte la maison. \q Akzib, la Ville-du-Mensonge, \q décevra les rois d’Israël.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo utatoa zawadi za kuagana \q kwa Moresheth-gathi; \q nyumba za Akzibu [zitakuwa] udanganyifu \q kwa wafalme wa Israeli.
